newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel chooses first astronaut for NASA mission.
newsitem.headline: Israel chooses first astronaut for NASA mission.

text.p: Officials have chosen a 40-year-old air force pilot to be the first Israeli to travel to outer space, they said on Wednesday.

An Israeli committee chose the pilot, an air force colonel trained as an engineer, to join a U.S. space shuttle mission late next year under an agreement with thr National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).
The pilot will serve as the mission's "payload specialist", overseeing an outer space experiment which Israel must propose and finance.
"The moment we decide on the experiment, the Americans will provide us with a date for the mission," said Abi Har-Even, director of the Israeli Space Agency.
He said NASA must give its approval for the experiment and for the astronaut, whom he described as "more than qualified". The United States will pay for the astronaut's training.
